correctness.rationale: For each orbit union R_S=S×{0,1}, an independent set selects at most one end per rung and assigns a proper 2-coloring to the used induced H-subgraph; conversely a 2-coloring selects an independent prism set. Thus alpha(G[R_S])=max size of an induced bipartite T⊆S. In the simplicial realization a layer-swap fixed point has equal barycentric coefficients at the two ends of each rung, so the fixed triangulation consists exactly of admissible midpoint simplices indexed by beta_H(S)<k. If H is bipartite, beta_H(S)=|S| and the fixed simplicial complex is the full (k−2)-skeleton; the Gaussian-free simplex skeleton top reduced homology has rank binom(m−1,k−1), is free, and the claimed wedge type follows from connectivity/Hurewicz-Whitehead, including k=2, k>m. The ladder k=3 Smith equality separately uses the known ambient Filakovský two-row-grid theorem. An independent exhaustive graph test over all simple graphs on one to four vertices (including all 64 graphs on four vertices) and thresholds/supports ran 1,098 exact rung-orbit comparisons. This finite test is corroboration, not the arbitrary-H proof.

value.rationale: A canonical geometric fixed-space model for every base graph and independence threshold is a structural equivariant-topology result, not simply another ambient Betti number. It determines an entire bipartite family of homotopy types and explains exact Smith total-Betti saturation for a natural ladder family, while the K3 counter-boundary isolates the bipartite simplification. Researchers can use the induced-bipartite-subgraph model without reconstructing the large prism complex.
residual_risks: Smith equality by itself would be a small corollary; value lies in the general fixed-space equivalence.
